_README: F&O TRANSACTION COSTS. Edit this file — the app re-reads it whenever it changes, no restart.
WHY YOU HAVE TO MAINTAIN THIS: statutory rates and exchange charges are set by circular, not
by any API. They have changed materially three times in recent years (STT on option sales
went from 0.0625% to 0.1%; NSE moved transaction charges off the old volume slabs). Rather
than quietly price your trades off stale numbers, the app reads them from here and tells you
on screen that they are unverified until you confirm them.
HOW TO VERIFY IN FIVE MINUTES — open ONE real contract note from your broker and check the
app's estimate against it. That single document contains every line below. If the totals
match, set "verified": true and the warning goes away. If they do not, edit the rate that is
wrong. A contract note is the authority here, not a website and not this file.
SOURCES if you would rather read the circulars:
STT          https://incometaxindia.gov.in  (Finance Act, Chapter VII)
NSE charges  https://www.nseindia.com/regulations/exchange-communication-circulars
BSE charges  https://www.bseindia.com/markets/MarketInfo/NoticesCirculars.aspx
Stamp duty   uniform across states since July 2020
EVERY RATE IS A FRACTION, NOT A PERCENTAGE. 0.001 means 0.1%.
brokerage: what YOUR broker charges per executed order, set separately for options and for
futures because the plans genuinely differ. OPTIONS at a discount broker are a FLAT ₹20 per
executed order with no percentage alternative — set pctOfTurnover to null. FUTURES are
usually '₹20 or 0.03%, whichever is lower', so both fields are set and the app takes the
lower. Full-service brokers charge a percentage on everything: set perOrder to null and
pctOfTurnover to their rate. Set perOrder to 0 if your broker is genuinely free.
Getting this backwards matters more than it looks. Applying a 0.03% alternative to options
makes a cheap weekly appear almost free to trade, when a flat ₹20 is in fact the single
largest charge on it.
THE FLAT FEE IS THE ONE THAT HURTS. ₹20 per order on a 75-lot NIFTY option costs 0.27 premium
points. On a 20-point out-of-the-money weekly that is 1.3% of the position PER LEG before any
tax has been charged — and the round trip starts you nearly 4% down. The app shows cost as a
percentage of premium for exactly this reason.
sttExercise is the rate charged on INTRINSIC VALUE when an in-the-money option is allowed to
expire instead of being squared off. It is charged to the buyer, and it is higher than the
rate on a sale (sttSell). Since the September 2019 amendment it applies to intrinsic value
rather than to the full settlement value, so it is no longer the account-ending trap it was
before then.
AND THAT HIGHER RATE DOES NOT MEAN YOU SHOULD ALWAYS SQUARE OFF — the app computes both routes
rather than following the folk rule. Selling saves 0.025% of intrinsic in STT but pays a whole
extra leg of exchange charges (0.035% of premium), GST on them, another ₹20 of brokerage and
the bid-ask spread. On a deep in-the-money option with no time value left those outweigh the
STT saving and expiring is cheaper. Squaring off wins once enough EXTRINSIC value remains to
cover the gap; the app reports exactly how much that is for your position.

brokerage.note: per executed order. When both fields are set the app charges the lower; null disables that field.

note: USED ONLY WHEN LIVE BID/ASK IS UNAVAILABLE, and the app says so when it falls back to it.
The bid-ask spread is usually the LARGEST cost in an option trade and the only one not
printed on the contract note. One tick is optimistic for anything but a near-the-money
weekly index option; far strikes routinely show five to twenty ticks.

_incomeTaxNote: Not modelled per trade, because it is not a per-trade cost. In India F&O profit is BUSINESS
income, taxed at your slab rate — there is no concessional capital-gains rate on it. Losses
can be carried forward eight years if the return is filed on time, and a tax audit may be
required above the turnover threshold. Everything this app reports is PRE-TAX.
